question: Should RFC 0013 formally include these optional lifecycle sidecars, or should aggregate recovery handoff and restored admission be specified separately from the SQLite artifact contract?
rationale: The author intentionally proposes a normative ownership split between core state owners and infrastructure hosts; documentation review cannot determine that product and architecture boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt the optional sidecars
options.body: Accept the three specifications as RFC 0013 follow-ons while retaining host ownership of ingress fencing, durable acceptance, wake, placement, and destruction.

options.title: Keep RFC 0013 artifact-only
options.body: Retain the completed RFC’s one-database snapshot boundary and move lifecycle coordination to a separate proposal or external host guidance.

options.title: Request a smaller seam
options.body: Accept only the minimum owner-facing invariants needed for future host work and defer the broader lifecycle contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt the optional sidecars
recommendation.body: Accept the three specifications as RFC 0013 follow-ons while retaining host ownership of ingress fencing, durable acceptance, wake, placement, and destruction.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied RFC context identifies this contributor’s upstream snapshot work as the primary implementation boundary being extended.
